user_questions.question: "Fix onboarding" does not say what is broken or what the outcome should be. The org has an Onboarding_Application__c object (Status__c: Submitted, Under Review, Approved, Onboarded). What should change: (a) applications getting stuck or lost in a status (alerts/escalation), (b) data captured on the application (fields/validation), (c) assignment of the application to a person, (d) something else? Please describe the desired outcome.
user_questions.simulated_answer: Onboarding apps get lost; applications in Submitted > 3 days should notify the onboarding manager.

user_questions.question: Who is the 'onboarding manager' to notify? Options: (a) the user in Onboarding_Application__c.Onboarding_Specialist__c (Lookup User, 'assigned by the Agent'); (b) a new public group 'Onboarding Managers' whose members you name (no role, queue, or group for this exists; 0 users have a Manager set); (c) the record owner. Recommendation: (b), because lost applications are likely the ones no specialist picked up.
user_questions.simulated_answer: No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: Entry check 'too vague' says ask when there is 'no desired outcome, or no identifiable business object'; 'Fix onboarding.' has an identifiable object (Onboarding_Application__c) but no outcome. The OR made this clear, but it is unclear whether the entry clarifying answer, which fixed the outcome but not the recipient persona, still leaves room for the one step-5 message (assumed yes, since the entry question 'does not use up the step 5 message').

Step 5 says to predict the answer and decide instead if 'no preference' is expected and the default is safe; with a simulated user whose intent is silent on the recipient, the prediction is always 'no preference', yet persona is an explicit Ask category. Guidance on which rule wins would help.

The narrowed I retry (required by the timeout rule) dropped established facts, and AskCoworker then proposed creating a field that exists; the skill does not say which facts must survive a narrowed retry.

AskCoworker wrong-claim counting: D1 made three wrong claims in one answer (only one custom field, no submitted-date field, no identity field) that all stem from one FLS-hidden describe; unclear whether that counts as one or three toward the 2/4 thresholds. Counted separately, which reached four with the I retry and allowed skipping R and T.
Tooling FlowDefinitionView fails (it is standard-API only, as the reference says), but the entry-check scan happens before the reference files are read, so the first attempt used the wrong API.
